:::{#thm-best-constant-step}
#### The best constant step length

In the setting of @thm-gd-quadratic-error,
let $\eigval_{\min}$ and $\eigval_{\max}$ be the smallest and largest eigenvalues of $\matr{S}$.
The bound's factor $\convrate(\steplen) = \max_i \abs{1 - \steplen\,\eigval_i}$
is smallest over $\steplen > 0$ at

$$
\steplen^* = \frac{2}{\eigval_{\min} + \eigval_{\max}},
$$

where

$$
\convrate(\steplen^*) = \frac{\condnum - 1}{\condnum + 1},
\qquad
\condnum = \condnum(\matr{S}),
$$

the [condition number](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-condition-number) of $\matr{S}$.

:::

::: proof

For $\steplen > 0$, each $1 - \steplen\,\eigval_i$ lies between
$u_{\min} \eqdef 1 - \steplen\,\eigval_{\max}$ and $u_{\max} \eqdef 1 - \steplen\,\eigval_{\min}$,
so $\abs{1 - \steplen\,\eigval_i} \le \max(u_{\max}, -u_{\min})$.
The two eigenvalues $\eigval_{\min}$ and $\eigval_{\max}$ are among the $\eigval_i$,
and $\abs{u_{\max}} \ge u_{\max}$ and $\abs{u_{\min}} \ge -u_{\min}$,
so the maximum is attained:

$$
\convrate(\steplen) = \max\paren{1 - \steplen\,\eigval_{\min},\ \steplen\,\eigval_{\max} - 1}.
$$

The first expression is strictly decreasing in $\steplen$ and the second is strictly increasing,
and they are equal when

$$
\ba
1 - \steplen\,\eigval_{\min} &= \steplen\,\eigval_{\max} - 1
&& \text{(set the two expressions equal)}
\\
2 &= \steplen\,(\eigval_{\min} + \eigval_{\max})
&& \text{(collect the terms in } \steplen \text{)}
\\
\steplen &= \frac{2}{\eigval_{\min} + \eigval_{\max}} = \steplen^*.
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

For $\steplen < \steplen^*$, $\convrate(\steplen)$ is at least the decreasing expression,
which exceeds its value at $\steplen^*$.
For $\steplen > \steplen^*$, $\convrate(\steplen)$ is at least the increasing expression,
which exceeds its value at $\steplen^*$.
So $\steplen^*$ is the minimizer, and

$$
\ba
\convrate(\steplen^*)
&= 1 - \frac{2\,\eigval_{\min}}{\eigval_{\min} + \eigval_{\max}}
&& \text{(first expression at } \steplen^* \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{\eigval_{\max} - \eigval_{\min}}{\eigval_{\max} + \eigval_{\min}}
&& \text{(common denominator)}
\\
&= \frac{\condnum - 1}{\condnum + 1}.
&& \text{(divide the numerator and denominator by } \eigval_{\min} \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
